name: PRDGenie WF6 - Judge sweep
_comment_active: Active, with its schedule node deliberately disabled: the demo environment is manual-only (PRD-E7 Q3). An inactive workflow has no webhook door at all (BUG-005/018).

parameters.content:
## WF6 - the judge sweep

**A second opinion that gates nothing.** Gemini 2.5 Flash reads a bounded random sample of
output the doer produced and says whether the source supports it. No case, no threshold, no
metric and no report figure reads any of it (E7-S5, verified by
`verify-judge-isolation.mjs`).

**The service draws the sample, not this workflow.** Opening a sweep IS taking the lock, in
one call, so two sweeps can never sample the same rows and inflate coverage.

**A sweep that gets no opinion is RECORDED as skipped**, with a reason from the closed set.
There is no fallback to OpenAI - a second opinion from the vendor that wrote the thing is
not a second opinion.

## Nightly, and off in the demo

PRD-E7 Q3: **nightly cron plus a manual trigger, and the demo environment is manual-only**
so a sweep can be shown on command.

The schedule node below is therefore **disabled in the shipped file**, deliberately and
visibly, rather than absent. It was proven to fire through itself first (E7-S5 TC6, dated in
`docs/traceability.md`): the interval was set to every minute, the workflow was watched
starting itself, and the file was restored.

Enable it by opening the node and switching it on - nothing else changes, and a cron sweep
records `trigger_source=cron` so it is never confused with a hand-picked one.

parameters.content:
## When Gemini does not answer

`WF0: judge` continues past its own failure so the NEXT node can record what happened. That
is the whole exemption: **the failure becomes a row**, not a silence.

A sweep where nothing came back closes as `skipped` with a reason from the closed set -
never as a clean sweep, and never by asking the doer instead. Drilled twice in E7-S5.

parameters.content:
## One call at a time, twelve seconds apart

**Nobody is waiting for this.** The judge gates nothing, so a sweep can afford to take five minutes where a PM waiting on a PRD cannot afford to take five seconds.

It exists because the provider meters requests per minute, and twenty-two calls in ninety seconds spends that meter in the first fifteen — which turns a bounded sample into a biased one: **the rows that got judged would be the rows that were drawn first**, not a random twenty-two. Pacing keeps the sample the thing it claims to be.

**Not a Wait node.** A Wait suspends the execution and drops the caller's connection; the sweep then finishes unheard, or dies holding the lock. A sleep inside a Code node keeps the run continuous.
